title: Context Fidelity Catalog and Seed Procedure
author: Asha Menon
content:
Summary
=======
This document defines a curated catalog of "context-fidelity" prompt cohorts and a repeatable, automated procedure for generating and versioning seed probes used by the eval harness, model onboarding, and regression triage teams. The goal is to produce seeds that exercise contextual sensitivity, priming behavior, and token-budget tradeoffs while ensuring reproducible measurement of fidelity-related regressions across model variants and quantization profiles.

Scope
-----
Applies to: prompt authors, evaluator engineers, model-onboarding owners, and quality-guardrails automation.
Excluded: ad-hoc user support prompts (those belong in product-driven prompt registries).

Definitions
-----------
- Context fidelity: the degree to which a model maintains instruction intent and response quality when context (priming, examples, history) changes.
- Seed: a single prompt instance (with metadata) used repeatedly across evals.
- Cohort: a named group of seeds that share a testing objective (e.g., "slot-anchored-multi-turn").
- Anchor prompt: a canonical prompt used as the base for synthetic augmentation and paraphrase generation.

Catalog: Cohorts and Targets
---------------------------
Below is the canonical catalog we maintain in the eval registry. Use this table to select the appropriate cohort for an onboarding campaign or regression sweep.

| Cohort ID | Purpose | Context Pattern | Fidelity target (RSI) | Token budget | Typical telemetry tags | Example anchor |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| CF-ANCH-MT | Multi-turn anchor sensitivity | 3-turn history + instruction | >= 0.92 | 256 | multi_turn, kv_cache_sensitive | "Plan a 3-step onboarding flow for a new user" |
| CF-PRIM-SHORT | Priming robustness (short) | 1-shot priming + single query | >= 0.95 | 64 | priming, short_ctx | "As an expert, summarize the paragraph:" |
| CF-PRIM-LONG | Priming robustness (long) | 5-shot priming + long context | >= 0.90 | 1024 | priming, long_ctx, cache_heavy | "You are a legal assistant. Provide key points:" |
| CF-SLOT-ANCH | Slot filling with distractors | template with 4 slots + noise | >= 0.91 | 192 | slot_filling, adversarial_noise | "Extract name, role, start_date, region from text:" |
| CF-FEWCLUSTER | Few-shot variability | 8-shot variable examples | >= 0.89 | 768 | fewshot, diversity | "Translate these examples and infer style:" |
| CF-STREAM-SEQ | Streaming/continuation fidelity | streaming tokens, functioncall-boundary | >= 0.93 | 512 | streaming, functioncall | "Continue the story preserving character voice:" |

Selection guidance
-------------------
- For latency-sensitive model families prefer CF-PRIM-SHORT or CF-ANCH-MT with reduced token budgets.
- For quantization regression analysis target CF-PRIM-LONG and CF-SLOT-ANCH to detect loss of long-context coherence and slot hallucination.
- Use CF-STREAM-SEQ for functioncall and streaming tail regressions.

Seed Generation Procedure (automated pipeline)
---------------------------------------------
1. Choose cohort (see Catalog) and select n_anchor anchors (default n_anchor=12).
2. For each anchor generate augmentations: paraphrase (2x), adversarial-noise insertion (1x), contextual-reorder (1x), synthetic-user-variant (3x).
3. Apply constraint filters: token budget (truncate or expand examples), anonymize PII, and ensure language-localization variants if cohort requires (en, es, fr).
4. Run classifier-based sensitivity checks: pass each augmented seed through the "prompt-sanity" classifier (threshold 0.6) to filter nonsensical augmentations.
5. Persist seeds to the eval registry with metadata: cohort_id, origin_anchor_id, augmentation_type, seed_version, creation_sha, and owner. See manifest YAML below.
6. Kick off small smoke eval against the shadow model (10 samples per seed) and compute RSI (Response Stability Index). If RSI < cohort target, flag for human review.
7. Approve seeds by reviewer group (applied-ml-evals) and promote seeds to "active" for continuous monitoring.

Automated QC checks and gating thresholds
----------------------------------------
- Response Stability Index (RSI): primary gate (computed as pairwise normalized similarity + instruction adherence score). Gate: pass if RSI >= cohort target.
- Embedding drift: mean cosine distance vs. anchor embedding must be <= 0.05 for paraphrase variants.
- Semantic F1 (slot cohorts): >= 0.88 for CF-SLOT-ANCH.
- Perplexity sanity: perplexity on baseline LMs must not exceed 3x median training perplexity for that cohort.
- Runtime checks: median latency on representative dedicated instance must be within 1.5x baseline for that cohort.

Seed manifest (example YAML saved in eval registry)
--------------------------------------------------
---
cohort_id: CF-PRIM-LONG
seed_version: "v1.3"
anchor_id: anchor-20260110-07
augmentation: paraphrase
language: en
token_budget: 1024
owner: "applied-ml-evals"
creation_sha: "a1b2c3d4"
labels:
  - priming
  - long_ctx
expected_rsi: "0.90"
metadata_sample: |
  You are an assistant specialized in financial compliance. Summarize the regulatory differences between jurisdictions X and Y.
---

Onboarding checklist for model promotion using these seeds
---------------------------------------------------------
1. Register model with model-onboarding system and attach target cohorts (min: CF-ANCH-MT, CF-PRIM-LONG).
2. Run full seed sweep (all cohorts) in shadow for at least 10k aggregate requests.
3. Verify automated QC passes (RSI, embedding drift, semantic F1).
4. Run human spot-checks: sample 50 seeds across cohorts, annotate for instruction adherence and hallucination. Requirement: >= 95% pass on instruction adherence.
5. If any cohort fails, open a triage ticket (label: regression-cohort-<id>) and attach diagnostic artifact set (seed IDs, model run logs, kv-cache traces).
6. Post-approval: schedule weekly rolling checks for the first 2 weeks, then daily for the first month post-promotion.

Regression triage quick-path
---------------------------
1. If CI or production alert reports an RSI drop >= 0.03 from baseline, automatically snapshot the failing seeds and route to the regression-triage queue.
2. Run pairwise comparison across model variants (full and quantized) and collect: token-level diffs, attention-heatmap excerpts, kv-cache hit/miss counts.
3. If quantized variant shows systematic degradation, run quant-shadow sweep (see quantization-profiles/quant-shadow-cohort-strategy-and-rollback-playbook-2026.json) and apply per-cohort hedging (e.g., pin CF-PRIM-LONG to higher precision until rollback).
4. Escalate to applied-ml senior oncall if human spot-check failure rate > 10% or if customer-impacting SLO breach detected.

Operational ownership and runbook links
-------------------------------------
- Owner: applied-ml-evals (primary), model-onboarding (secondary).
- Oncall: applied-ml-regression (pager duty).
- Runbooks: see eval-harness/runbooks for scheduling and failure recovery procedures.

Appendix A — CLI snippets
-------------------------
Create seed manifest:
$ rl eval seed create --cohort CF-PRIM-LONG --from-anchor anchor-20260110-07 --paraphrases 2 --out manifest.yaml
Upload and kick smoke test:
$ rl eval seed upload --manifest manifest.yaml --kick-smoke
Query seed RSI report:
$ rl eval report rsi --cohort CF-PRIM-LONG --since 2026-01-01

Appendix B — Example diagnostic JSON (single seed run)
-----------------------------------------------------
{
  "seed_id": "cf-primlong-20260110-07-p1",
  "model": "redwood-rlhf-12b-v2",
  "rsi": "0.87",
  "embedding_cosine": "0.038",
  "latency_ms": "78",
  "notes": "paraphrase reduced instruction adherence; escalate for manual review"
}
